classification.difficultyReason: Interpret each shaded region, choose discs or washers for the specified axis, rearrange the curve and obtain simple bounds using the taught procedure.

content.prompt:
Find the volume of the solid generated by rotating each region about:

 i the $x$-axis

 ii the $y$-axis

In some cases, a subtraction of volumes will be necessary.

spec.description: Arrowed parabola and axes; first-quadrant region under the parabola ends at x=2. No grid or additional ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; shaded region is permanent.

answer.worked:
Outer radius $2$, inner radius $\sqrt y$; $0\le y\le4$.

$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^4(4-y)\,dy\\V&=\pi\left[4y-\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_0^4\\V&=8\pi\text{ u}^3\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Line through the origin with arrows at both ends; shaded triangle bounded by the line, y-axis and y=5. Only 5 is labelled.

answer.worked:
Outer radius $5$, inner radius $5x$; $0\le x\le1$.

$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^1(25-25x^2)\,dx\\V&=25\pi\left[x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1\\V&=\frac{50\pi}{3}\text{ u}^3\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Right-opening parabola with arrows on both branches; shaded first-quadrant region below its upper branch, ending at x=4.

answer.worked:
Outer radius $4$, inner radius $y^2$; $0\le y\le2$.

$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^2(16-y^4)\,dy\\V&=\pi\left[16y-\frac{y^5}{5}\right]_0^2\\V&=\frac{128\pi}{5}\text{ u}^3\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex at (0,3), both arms arrowed. Region between the y-axis, parabola and y=4 is shaded. Equation has a curved pointer to the right arm.

answer.worked:
Outer radius $4$, inner radius $x^2+3$; $0\le x\le1$.

$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^1\bigl(16-(x^2+3)^2\bigr)\,dx\\V&=\pi\int_0^1(7-6x^2-x^4)\,dx\\V&=\pi\left[7x-2x^3-\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^1\\V&=\frac{24\pi}{5}\text{ u}^3\end{aligned}$$
